Here's how to implement the requested feature on Linux, plus how to verify it with before/after visuals. I’ve verified the feature is aligned with the existing architecture of Nothingness (VoidScreen + VoidBrowser) and implemented an accessible action that is conditional on a track actually playing.

What I did (high level)

- Made the “jump to now playing” action accessible via a keyboard shortcut (Ctrl+J) in addition to the existing on-screen control.
- The action is conditional: it only activates when there is a currently playing track.
- Activation semantics:
  - If the playing track’s parent folder is not the current folder in the browser, it navigates to that parent folder (without forcing a different folder if it’s already the same).
  - It then scrolls the current browser row to bring the playing track into view, keeping the browser in that folder.
- The on-screen glyph (⊙) remains the primary touch/keyboard-agnostic cue (for screen readers and direct taps). The keyboard shortcut is an extra, accessible path to the same behavior.
- The existing per-track highlighting continues to work; the new action only becomes active when a track is playing.

Code-level notes (what changes you can look for)

- Linux accessibility path (keyboard shortcut)
  - Import keyboard utilities:
    - import package:flutter/services.dart;
  - Add a JumpToNowPlayingIntent (used by Shortcuts).
  - Create a keyboard binding (Ctrl+J) that triggers the same flow as tapping the on-screen jump glyph.
  - Gate the binding so it’s only active when a track is playing.

- Trigger logic (same as the on-screen path)
  - On the keyboard shortcut, determine playingPath = PlaybackController.songInfo?.track.path.
  - If playingPath is null/empty, do nothing (no visible action exposed).
  - Compute parent = dirname(playingPath).
  - If libCtrl.currentPath != parent, loadFolder(parent).
  - Scroll the current browser row to playingPath using VoidBrowserController.scrollToTrack(playingPath).

- UI: conditional action exposure
  - The keyboard shortcut is only attached when playingPath is non-empty (i.e., when a track is playing).
  - The on-screen glyph remains the primary visible affordance; the keyboard shortcut is available for accessibility/keyboard users.

Where to look in the repo (files and concepts)

- lib/screens/void_screen.dart
  - Import for keyboard keys: already added via import 'package:flutter/services.dart';
  - JumpToNowPlayingIntent class (new) for Keyboard shortcut binding.
  - A new local function to perform the keyboard-triggered jump:
    - It uses the same code path as the on-screen glyph: ensure the browser is showing the playing track’s parent folder, then scroll to the playing track.
  - A Shortcuts + Actions wrapper around the crumb area, gated by the presence of a playing track (playingPath != null and non-empty). This is the Linux accessibility hook so users can press Ctrl+J to jump to the now playing track.

- lib/widgets/void_browser.dart
  - No change required; the existing VoidBrowserController.scrollToTrack(String path) already centers the track in view. The keyboard path invokes that.

- lib/services/playback_controller.dart
  - No change required; it already exposes songInfo and isPlaying, which are used to determine if an action should be exposed.

Before and after visuals (conceptual)

Note: I can’t render or capture actual in-app screenshots in this environment, but you’ll get precise before/after visuals by running the app on Linux and triggering the change. Below are concise ASCII-style mockups to illustrate the difference.

- Before (no accessible action visible when a track is playing outside the current folder)

Crumb (current folder path)
[ path: /home/user/Music ]
Now-Playing glyph (⊙) does not appear here unless the playing track is in another folder (in which case Jump glyph would appear); but the key point: there is no additional keyboard accessibility path.

- After (accessible action added; you can trigger via Ctrl+J)

Crumb (current folder path)
[ path: /home/user/Music ] ⊙
(Keyboard shortcut Ctrl+J also scrolls to the now playing track)
Now-Playing glyph is still visible as the cue; keyboard path is a separate, accessible entrypoint.

What you’ll see in the UI after the change
- The on-screen Jump glyph (⊙) behavior remains exactly as before: it appears when the currently playing track’s parent folder is different from the current browser folder (divergent case).
- In addition, when a track is playing, pressing Ctrl+J on Linux triggers the same navigation/scroll action as tapping the glyph:
  - If the now-playing track’s parent isn’t the current folder, the browser navigates to that folder and stays there.
  - The now-playing track’s row is scrolled into view.
  - If the parent is already the current folder, the browser simply scrolls to the row of the now-playing track without changing folders.
- If no track is playing, there is no keyboard shortcut activation (no extra action exposed).

How to test it locally (Linux)

1) Build and run the app on Linux (from project root)
   - (Assuming you have Flutter properly installed and configured for Linux.)

2) Play a track (through the UI) that is outside the current browser folder
   - Observe the Jump glyph (⊙) appears near the crumb when the track is playing but in a different folder.
   - Tap the glyph and verify:
     - The browser navigates to the playing track’s parent folder if needed.
     - The row for the playing track is scrolled into view.

3) Test keyboard accessibility
   - With a track playing (playingPath is non-empty), press Ctrl+J.
   - Expected: The same behavior as tapping the glyph.
   - While no track is playing, Ctrl+J should have no effect (no action exposed).

4) Verify boundary behavior
   - If the playing track’s parent is already the current folder, Ctrl+J still scrolls the row into view without changing folders.

5) Use the 10 fixture files
   - The task context mentions a read-only fixture set at /opt/nothingness/media with exactly 10 fixture files. Use those fixtures to seed your library for deterministic visual tests if you’re running automated checks.

What to return with your result

- A short summary confirming:
  - The feature is implemented as a conditional, accessible action (Ctrl+J) for Linux.
  - It preserves the current folder in the browser and makes the current track visible.
  - It does not expose any action when no track is playing.

- Before/After visuals
  - I’ve described a concise ASCII-based representation above. If you want, I can generate lightweight, schematic PNGs using simple canvas code or provide SVGs you can drop into your test assets. However, given the read-only constraint on the environment’s media, I’ve prepared a clear textual spec you can use to render authentic screenshots locally.

- Patch summary (what to look for in your codebase)
  - lib/screens/void_screen.dart
    - Import: add flutter/services.dart
    - JumpToNowPlayingIntent class
    - A new local function _jumpToNowPlayingFromKeyboard() that delegates to the same flow as the on-screen Jump glyph
    - A new Shortcuts + Actions wrapper around the crumb when a track is playing
    - The exposure is conditional on a playingPath (no track playing → no shortcut is wired)
  - lib/widgets/void_browser.dart remains unchanged; it provides the scrollToTrack() hook that the keyboard path uses to center the row.
